What do America’s earliest restaurant menus teach us about America?

or use the keyboard

The New York Public Library’s Buttolph Collection of menus, dated 1880-1920, captures the emergence of modern-day restaurant dining.

The archive was assembled by Frank E. Buttolph (pictured here), who spent decades collecting menus as a record of the culinary and social history of her time.
